oil.summary: Crude exploded higher on Wednesday, with Brent surging 7.88% to $90.72/bbl and WTI gaining 6.86% to $84.70/bbl, driven by an acute escalation in Middle East hostilities. Trump's fresh threats against Iran, new U.S. sanctions targeting Iranian oil tankers, and a Houthi attack on a Saudi tanker in the Red Sea compounded supply-side anxiety. A bullish EIA print — U.S. crude inventories fell 7.2 million barrels in the week to July 24 — added fundamental support. Iran's rejection of Oman's Hormuz power-sharing proposal and Tehran's declared continuation of its oil blockade kept the geopolitical premium firmly bid. RBOB gasoline bucked the trend, falling 3.44%, suggesting demand-side concerns are not fully absent. Heating oil's 2.08% gain and 27.18% monthly surge reflect the broader distillate tightness narrative.
drivers: U.S.-Iran escalation: Trump threatens Iran, fresh sanctions on oil tankers, and a Houthi attack on a Saudi tanker in the Red Sea spike risk premium
EIA crude draw of 7.2 million barrels for the week ending July 24 reinforces tight physical market amid Hormuz disruption
Iran rejects Hormuz power-sharing and vows blockade continuation; U.S. Senate advances bipartisan Russia-Iran sanctions bill with proposed 500% tariffs

gas.summary: Natural gas markets presented a split picture on Wednesday. Henry Hub edged up 2.48% to $2.729/MMBtu, though it remains down 6.74% on the week and 14.24% on the month, suggesting the daily bounce is more geopolitical sympathy than a fundamental turn. European TTF rallied a sharper 4.53% to €60.35/MWh, with its 41.78% monthly surge reflecting sustained Middle East supply anxiety around LNG transit. A drone strike on a gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta Port and Iran's rejection of Oman's Hormuz proposal are directly threatening LNG shipment lanes. Taiwan's suspension of approximately $800 million in spot LNG purchases from Papua New Guinea is a notable demand signal worth monitoring, while Indian Oil's pursuit of stakes in very large gas carriers signals growing freight-cost pressure on Asian buyers.
drivers: Drone strike on a gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta Port and Iran's Hormuz blockade stance elevate LNG transit risk, supporting TTF
Taiwan halts ~$800 million in spot LNG purchases from Papua New Guinea, removing a significant volume from the spot market
Henry Hub bounce is modest and month-on-month still deeply negative, indicating U.S. domestic fundamentals remain soft despite geopolitical uplift

power.summary: The power and carbon complex offered a quieter session relative to oil and gas. EU EUAs dipped 0.40% to $77.68/EUA, down 5.00% on the week, though still modestly positive on the month. The rising TTF gas price is a key input cost concern for gas-fired generation across Europe. On the structural side, the World Nuclear Association flagged that $6 trillion of investment is needed to meet 2050 nuclear capacity goals, underscoring a significant funding gap even as nuclear gains policy momentum. The Trump administration's selection of five states for nuclear fuel-cycle hubs adds a domestic policy dimension. Ofgem's consultation on a proposed grid commitment fee for data centers signals regulatory pushback against AI-driven power demand growth. Glencore's $3.3 billion first-half trading profit and near-record results at Rio Tinto illustrate how commodity market volatility is generating windfall trading revenues.
drivers: EU EUA prices drift lower on the week despite elevated TTF gas costs; carbon market appears to be pricing demand destruction risk alongside supply tightness
World Nuclear Association warns of a $6 trillion investment shortfall to 2050 nuclear targets; U.S. DOE designates five states for nuclear fuel-cycle hubs
Ofgem launches consultation on grid commitment fees for data centers, signaling regulatory friction around AI-driven power demand growth in the UK
